pairs: And so I make known to you,
the Gospel that I preached to you,
if you hold to the understanding that I preached to you,
Tradidi enim vobis in primis quod et accepi:
For I handed on to you, first of all,
quoniam Christus mortuus est pro peccatis nostris secundum Scripturas:
what I also received: that Christ died for our sins, according to the Scriptures;
et quia resurrexit tertia die secundum Scripturas:
and that he rose again on the third day, according to the Scriptures;
and that he was seen by Cephas,
and after that by the eleven.
deinde visus est plus quam quingentis fratribus simul:
Next he was seen by more than five hundred brothers at one time,
ex quibus multi manent usque adhuc,
many of whom remain, even to the present time,
Next, he was seen by James,
he was seen also by me,
as if I were someone born at the wrong time.
For I am the least of the Apostles.
qui non sum dignus vocari Apostolus,
I am not worthy to be called an Apostle,
because I persecuted the Church of God.
Gratia autem Dei sum id quod sum,
But, by the grace of God, I am what I am.
et gratia ejus in me vacua non fuit,
And his grace in me has not been empty,
since I have labored more abundantly than all of them.
but the grace of God within me.
Si autem Christus prædicatur quod resurrexit a mortuis,
that he rose again from the dead,
how is it that some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
Si autem resurrectio mortuorum non est:
For if there is no resurrection of the dead,
And if Christ has not risen,
and your faith is also useless.
invenimur autem et falsi testes Dei:
Then, too, we would be found to be false witnesses of God,
quoniam testimonium diximus adversus Deum quod suscitaverit Christum,
because we would have given testimony against God, saying that he had raised up Christ,
when he had not raised him up, if,
indeed, the dead do not rise again.
For if the dead do not rise again,
then neither has Christ risen again.
But if Christ has not risen,
adhuc enim estis in peccatis vestris.
for you would still be in your sins.
those who have fallen asleep in Christ would have perished.
Si in hac vita tantum in Christo sperantes sumus,
If we have hope in Christ for this life only,
then we are more miserable than all men.
Nunc autem Christus resurrexit a mortuis primitiæ dormientium,
But now Christ has risen again from the dead, as the first-fruits of those who sleep.
For certainly, death came through a man. And so,
the resurrection of the dead came through a man
Et sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur,
And just as in Adam all die,
ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur.
so also in Christ all will be brought to life,
but each one in his proper order: Christ,
and next, those who are of Christ,
who have believed in his advent.
cum tradiderit regnum Deo et Patri,
when he will have handed over the kingdom to God the Father,
when he will have emptied all principality,
Oportet autem illum regnare donec ponat omnes inimicos sub pedibus ejus.
For it is necessary for him to reign, until he has set all his enemies under his feet.
Lastly, the enemy called death shall be destroyed.
For he has subjected all things under his feet.
“All things have been subjected to him,”
sine dubio præter eum qui subjecit ei omnia.
without doubt he does not include the One who has subjected all things to him.
Cum autem subjecta fuerint illi omnia:
And when all things will have been subjected to him,
tunc et ipse Filius subjectus erit ei, qui subjecit sibi omnia,
then even the Son himself will be subjected to the One who subjected all things to him,
ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus.
so that God may be all in all.
Alioquin quid facient qui baptizantur pro mortuis,
what will those who are being baptized for the dead do,
if the dead do not rise again at all?
Why then are they being baptized for them?
ut quid et nos periclitamur omni hora?
Why also do we endure trials every hour?
Daily I die, by means of your boasting,
quam habeo in Christo Jesu Domino nostro.
you whom I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Si secundum hominem ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi,
If, according to man, I fought with the beasts at Ephesus,
if the dead do not rise again?
and do not be willing to sin.
For certain persons have an ignorance of God.
I say this to you with respect.
“How do the dead rise again?” or,
“What type of body do they return with?”
What you sow cannot be brought back to life,
et quod seminas, non corpus, quod futurum est,
And what you sow is not the body that will be in the future,
Deus autem dat illi corpus sicut vult:
For God gives it a body according to his will,
and according to each seed’s proper body.
Not all flesh is the same flesh.
But one is indeed of men,
Et corpora cælestia, et corpora terrestria:
Also, there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies.
But while the one, certainly, has the glory of heaven,
the other has the glory of earth.
One has the brightness of the sun,
another the brightness of the moon,
and another the brightness of the stars.
Stella enim a stella differt in claritate:
For even star differs from star in brightness.
So it is also with the resurrection of the dead.
Seminatur in corruptione, surget in incorruptione.
What is sown in corruption shall rise to incorruption.
Seminatur in ignobilitate, surget in gloria:
What is sown in dishonor shall rise to glory.
seminatur in infirmitate, surget in virtute:
What is sown in weakness shall rise to power.
seminatur corpus animale, surget corpus spiritale.
What is sown with an animal body shall rise with a spiritual body.
If there is an animal body,
est et spiritale, sicut scriptum est:
there is also a spiritual one.
Factus est primus homo Adam in animam viventem,
Just as it was written that the first man, Adam, was made with a living soul,
so shall the last Adam be made with a spirit brought back to life.
Sed non prius quod spiritale est,
So what is, at first, not spiritual,
sed quod animale: deinde quod spiritale.
Such things as are like the earth are earthly;
et qualis cælestis, tales et cælestes.
and such things as are like the heavens are heavenly.
just as we have carried the image of what is earthly,
let us also carry the image of what is heavenly.
quia caro et sanguis regnum Dei possidere non possunt:
because flesh and blood is not able to possess the kingdom of God;
neither will what is corrupt possess what is incorrupt.
Behold, I tell you a mystery.
Certainly, we shall all rise again,
but we shall not all be transformed:
in ictu oculi, in novissima tuba:
in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.
and the dead will rise up, incorruptible.
Oportet enim corruptibile hoc induere incorruptionem:
Thus, it is necessary for this corruptibility to be clothed with incorruptibility,
and for this mortality to be clothed with immortality.
Cum autem mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem,
And when this mortality has been clothed with immortality,
tunc fiet sermo, qui scriptus est:
then the word that was written shall occur:
O death, where is your sting?”
Now the sting of death is sin,
and the power of sin is the law.
qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum.
who has given us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
abounding always in the work of the Lord,
scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino.
knowing that your labor is not useless in the Lord.
